description: The pack-sire of the volcanic wolves. When it roars, the mountain answers, and the ash begins to fall.
lore: [[characters/54bead23|Osric]] wanted a fire he would not have to feed. He is a smith, and new — he still counts in living years and lets people correct him — and he had worked out that a man who spends his life on fuel should go and look at ground that is already hot. So he went up to the caldera with a rule and a notebook, and came back with three days of good measurements and one evening he does not offer around.

The sire is enormous, black as cooled slag, veined orange through the chest and legs, smoke standing off its shoulders in a plume you can see from the col. At dusk it called, and the pack answered off the slopes one voice at a time, in an order, and Osric counted seven. Then it called once more into a gap in the order and waited. Then again. Six times into the same gap, unhurried, the way you knock at a door you have every reason to think is answered. Then it lay down in the ash.

He understood the gap. Anyone who has kept anything here does: something up that mountain went [[lore/the_quiet|Quiet]], and the count it belonged to has not been corrected and will not be. Osric built his forge on the meadow side instead, where the wood comes in from three hours out and every fire is somebody's labour. He does not tell people the caldera was dangerous. He tells them it was occupied.
gm_notes: Shipped description adopted verbatim. Companion to magma_wolf: the pack arrives one by one, the sire keeps the roll. The sire is not grieving in any way it could name — it is a stage-three animal running a count, and the count has a hole in it. Osric's want (heat without fuel) and his loss (he gave it up) carry the record; he is the least-used of the living cast and the only one who would climb a volcano for a practical reason. Do not connect the missing voice to anything east of the caldera. No stone or leavings bound yet.
